Interface ServerFilterSpec

All Superinterfaces:
RouteFilterSpec<ServerFilterSpec>
public sealed interface ServerFilterSpec extends RouteFilterSpec<ServerFilterSpec>
A server filter declared with HttpRouteBuilder.serverFilter(String...): the functional form of a @ServerFilter bean, whose before and after filters are its @RequestFilter and @ResponseFilter methods. 
routes.serverFilter("/**").order(100).beforeReplacing((request, propagatedContext) -> {
    propagatedContext.add(new MdcPropagationContext(Map.of("path", request.getPath())));
    return null;
});

Like a @ServerFilter bean, it filters every request whose path matches one of its patterns, and whose method is one of its methods(HttpMethod...), if it has any: the requests to controllers, to handler routes, to static resources, and the requests no route matches, e.g. a 404 or a 405. It is global wherever it is declared: in any HttpRoutes bean, and in a HttpRouteGroup, whose prefix and filters do not apply to it.

It runs with the filter beans, ordered by order(int), like a filter bean ordered by @Order: a lower order runs first on the request and last on the response. Its default order is 0, the order of a @ServerFilter bean without an order. Like between filter beans, the order is the only guarantee: set it to run before or after a filter bean. The filters of the route groups and of the route run after every server filter, closest to the route. The request filters of one server filter run in the order they are declared, and so do its response filters; they also filter the response a request filter of the same server filter answered with.

Like the request filters of a @ServerFilter bean annotated @PreMatching, its request filters can run before the route is matched, and change the request that is matched, see preMatching().

Like the patterns of a @ServerFilter, the patterns are under micronaut.server.context-path, unless they start with it or appendContextPath(boolean) says otherwise. Each call of HttpRouteBuilder.serverFilter(String...) declares a new server filter: declaring the same one twice filters the requests twice.

    • preMatching

      ServerFilterSpec preMatching()
      Run the request filters before the route is matched, like @RequestFilter methods annotated @PreMatching: the route is matched with the request they continue with, e.g. with the URI they changed in place or the method of the request they returned, see ReplacingRouteRequestFilter. They run with the pre-matching filter beans, ordered by order(int), before the filters that run once the route is matched, and they filter the requests of the patterns and methods, as they were received, including those no route matches. The patterns and methods select the filter before the request filters run. 
      routes.serverFilter("/legacy/**").preMatching().beforeReplacing(request -> {
    request.uri(URI.create(request.getPath().replaceFirst("/legacy", "/api")));
    return null;
});

      Its response filters filter every response: the response a request filter answered with before the route was matched, like @ResponseFilter methods annotated @PreMatching, and otherwise the response of the route, like @ResponseFilter methods, ordered by order(int) with the filter beans. They filter each response once.
